# SakuBelajar — exercise brief

This is a synthetic planning exercise, not an actual organization, field study or competition entry. All supplied facts are limited to this brief.

The proposed idea is a locally accessible learning-pack service for a vocational course. Lecturers prepare small downloadable course packs. Students synchronize when a suitable connection is available and then read the packs offline. A coordinator manages versions and reports unresolved access problems. The team has an early idea only; no implemented app, signed partner, measured learning benefit, market survey or financial results are supplied.

The intended buyer/operator arrangement is unsettled. One possible arrangement is a course department funding coordination; another is a cooperative arrangement among participating instructors. The team has not chosen a price or device platform. The essay should help a judge understand the proposed final service and a credible first implementation, with later expansion beyond the first course. The team can use clearly labelled planning assumptions after discussing material choices with the user.

The user prefers connected Indonesian prose, an evidence-supported problem-first opening, a clear explanation of the whole service and compact implementation reasoning. They do not want a catalogue of features, a giant business-plan dossier or repeated statements that everything needs validation.
